title: Shared Excel formulas are lost for dependent formula cells

evidence.quote: const formula = fNode ? textOf(fNode) : undefined; ... if (formula) entry.f = `=${formula}`;
A single cell: display value, plus the formula when the cell is computed.

reasoning: Excel commonly stores shared formulas with text only on the anchor cell and empty f elements on dependent cells, for example f t="shared" si="0". This parser only records a formula when the f element has text, so dependent formula cells are modeled as plain cached values. Formula removal or formula-vs-value changes on those cells can be invisible when the cached display value is unchanged, violating the model contract that computed cells include f.
recommendation: Track shared formula definitions while parsing a worksheet and assign a formula representation to every shared-formula cell, preferably by expanding the anchor formula relative to each cell reference. At minimum, preserve a stable shared-formula marker so formula cells do not become indistinguishable from literal values.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The formula test helper emits only inline formula text, so the current tests never exercise empty shared-formula f nodes or dependent cells in a shared formula range.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an .xlsx worksheet fixture with B2 containing `<f t="shared" ref="B2:B3" si="0">A2*2</f>` and B3 containing `<f t="shared" si="0"/><v>6</v>`, then assert B3 includes an f value and diffModels detects formula removal/change for B3.
minimumFixScope: Update parseWorksheet in packages/core/src/adapters/excel/parse.ts and add shared-formula fixture support or raw worksheet fixture coverage in packages/core/test/excel.test.ts.
